title: Accounting Agents research corpus
mission: A public, read-only research corpus that helps people and agents find, understand, and reuse the information needed to build accounting agents.
coverage_note: The goal is exhaustive coverage. This release adds 28 source-checked references and five reading collections to an inherited research base. Jurisdiction, industry, empirical deployment, and data-interface coverage remain uneven.
review_note: The 716 inherited records retain their migration review status and historical provenance. The September 7 expansion records AI-assisted checks of 28 original source pages and five editorial collections, with scope and evidence on each record. Source checks are not professional review, independent replication, or live-system validation.
rights_note: Project-created factual metadata is CC0 1.0. Original editorial content is CC BY 4.0. Software is MIT. External source content is not redistributed or licensed by this project; access is not permission for training or reuse.
coverage_priorities: Reverify inherited source URLs, editions, effective dates, supersession, and evidence classifications; keep new release-specific checks current.
Add jurisdiction-specific accounting, audit, tax, payroll, and public-sector authorities.
Deepen transaction-level evidence, ERP pagination and completeness contracts, bank interfaces, and worked accounting examples beyond the initial standards and interface references.
Add independent empirical research, failed deployments, negative results, and reproducible datasets.
Record publisher reuse permissions, machine-readable licenses, and lawful full-text availability.
Develop industry-specific coverage for banking, insurance, healthcare, nonprofit, and government accounting.
